name: Gear / direction / pairing status word

enum.4: Reversing — motor is being commanded to run in reverse
enum.5: Rolling — the wheel/vehicle is currently in motion

explain: Little-endian 16-bit word formed from payload bytes 0-1 (arg[2]/arg[3]) of the id-226 dashboard frame; carries gear, drive mode, motion and pairing flags read every telemetry cycle.
source: worthless:jadx/sources/com/rcplusplus/fdandroid/data/FardriverTelemetry.java#L18 (gear:Int, name only — Worthless models gear as a plain scalar, not this bit-packed word, so it does not corroborate the packing itself)
notes: Bits 0-1 pack the 2-bit gear value (0-3, GraphPage.cs#L1516 `m_gear = arg[2] & 3`); bits 2-3 pack a 2-bit drive/XS-control mode (`(arg[2]>>2)&3`); bit 6 is unused in the decompiled source. In the high byte (arg[3]), bits 11-12 (word-relative) pack a 2-bit PassOk/unlock-progress code (`(arg[3]&0x18)>>3`, GraphPage.cs#L1548) and bit 15 is `function_state` (`(arg[3]&0x80)!=0`, GraphPage.cs#L1552); bits 8-10 and 13-14 are unused/unconfirmed. decode_telemetry() returns the raw 16-bit word for bitfield entries — callers must mask these multi-bit sub-fields themselves; this schema has no bit-mask type to isolate them as separate scalar keys.

name: Fault / stop status word

enum.4: Over-voltage alarm (if status_word_2 bit 15 set) / Under-voltage alarm (otherwise)
enum.10: Phase short-circuit fault (if status_word_1 bit 11 clear) / Phase-lost alarm (if set)
enum.15: Stop state active (App.Stop) — not one of the 15 numbered faults above

explain: Little-endian 16-bit word formed from payload bytes 2-3 (arg[4]/arg[5]) of the id-226 dashboard frame; each low bit is a numbered fault the official app concatenates into its on-screen alarm message.
source: worthless:jadx/sources/com/rcplusplus/fdandroid/data/FaultEntry.java#L20-L21 (errorFlags1/errorFlags2: Int — structurally corroborates two separate fault-flag integer words, not the exact bit-for-bit packing or a single merged word)
notes: Official source keeps this as two separate bytes, arg[4] (bits 0-7 here) and arg[5] (bits 8-14, plus bit 15 = the stop flag, here); this entry merges them into one little-endian u16 purely so decode_telemetry can slice it with the schema's fixed-width numeric types — bit numbering above is relative to the merged word, not the original per-byte numbering in the fault-message text (which restarts at 1 per byte and skips '16.Brake Alarm', a different frame's field: motor_stop_state, id 250/cmd 0xB2). Bits 4 and 10's exact meaning depends on status_word_2 (frame 0xB3 offset 4) bit 15 and status_word_1 (frame 0xB3 offset 2) bit 11 respectively, both cited above.

name: Modulation index
explain: PWM modulation depth, raw byte divided by 128 to give a 0-1(ish) ratio; higher values mean the controller is driving closer to its voltage ceiling.
source: worthless:jadx/sources/com/rcplusplus/fdandroid/data/FardriverTelemetry.java#L19 (modulation: Float, exact field-name match — Worthless states no unit or scale for this field, only the name and that it is a Float)
notes: Fix round 1, finding 3: downgraded from medium — the field-name match is exact, but Worthless's declaration is a bare `Float` with no unit/scale documented anywhere in the decompiled Kotlin source, so it does not independently corroborate the 0-1(ish) ratio or the 1/128 scale above.

name: Motor rotation speed
explain: Motor's measured electrical rotation speed, read as a signed 16-bit little-endian word so a reversed direction can show as negative.
source: worthless:jadx/sources/com/rcplusplus/fdandroid/data/FardriverTelemetry.java#L24 (rpm: Float — the field name itself is the unit, 'rpm' being an abbreviation of 'revolutions per minute'; kept at medium confidence on that basis, per fix round 1 finding 3's ruling)
notes: ParaPage.cs's own ReadParaMeter handler decodes the identical two bytes as App.rotation via an UNSIGNED cast (`(ushort)(arg[9]*256+arg[8])`, ParaPage.cs#L895); GraphPage.cs's dashboard handler decodes them SIGNED (`(short)(...)`, stored in m_MeasureSpeed). This entry follows the signed (GraphPage) interpretation since that is the page that actually renders live rider telemetry; docs/protocol.md's earlier §4.1 worked example already treats these bytes as unsigned for a purely-positive 1500rpm value, which is consistent either way (positive values decode identically signed or unsigned).

name: Battery/bus voltage
explain: Battery pack voltage as measured by the controller, raw value in tenths of a volt.
source: worthless:jadx/sources/com/rcplusplus/fdandroid/data/FardriverTelemetry.java#L30 (voltage: Float — the field name itself is the unit description, 'voltage' meaning volts by definition; kept at medium confidence on that basis, per fix round 1 finding 3's ruling)

name: Battery/bus (line) current
explain: Line current drawn from/returned to the battery, raw value in quarter-amp counts; sign indicates regen vs. drive.
source: worthless:jadx/sources/com/rcplusplus/fdandroid/data/FardriverTelemetry.java#L17 (current: Float, exact field-name match — Worthless states no unit for this field; do not assume amps from the name alone)
notes: Fix round 1, finding 3: downgraded from medium — 'current' is an exact field-name match but, unlike 'voltage'/'rpm', the bare word does not itself specify a unit (amps vs. milliamps vs. a raw ADC count are all equally consistent with the name), and Worthless's `Float` declaration states no unit either.

name: Throttle depth, raw ADC counts
explain: Raw throttle-position reading the controller reports back, displayed by the app as an unscaled count alongside the calibrated throttle voltage.
source: worthless:jadx/sources/com/rcplusplus/fdandroid/data/FardriverTelemetry.java#L28 (throttleRaw: Int, exact field-name match — Worthless states no unit/scale; 'raw' confirms it's unscaled but not that the two apps' raw counts share the same ADC range/resolution)
notes: Fix round 1, finding 3: downgraded from medium — the name match is exact but doesn't establish a shared numeric unit, since 'raw counts' isn't itself a physical unit (unlike 'voltage'/'rpm') and could differ in scale between the two apps' ADC front-ends.

name: Throttle voltage
explain: Calibrated throttle signal voltage, raw value in hundredths of a volt; updates once per full telemetry cycle rather than every frame.
source: worthless:jadx/sources/com/rcplusplus/fdandroid/data/FardriverTelemetry.java#L29 (throttleVoltage: Float, exact field-name match — Worthless states no scale, and per fix round 1 finding 3's ruling this compound name is treated like 'current'/'modulation', not like the bare 'voltage' field, since 'throttleVoltage' names a derived/calibrated signal whose scale isn't self-evident from the name)
notes: This is logical id 130 in ParaPage.cs's FlashReadAddr table (index 25 of 55, ParaPage.cs#L177-184), so cmd = 0x80|25 = 0x99. Unlike ids 226/232/238 (frames 0x80-0x82), which the controller re-sends every 7th frame, id 130 appears once per full 55-frame cycle — the throttle voltage updates less often than the other electrical readings, matching its role as a calibration/diagnostic reading rather than a fast control-loop input. Fix round 1, finding 3: downgraded from medium — see source annotation.

name: Global status word 1

enum.8: Seat/bucket-switch confirmed OK (clear = warning icon shown)
enum.11: Phase-lost condition present (changes fault_status_word bit 10's meaning to Phase-lost)

explain: Global_state1 in the decompiled source: a 16-bit status word read from the id-214 frame that several other fault/UI decisions branch on.

name: Global status word 2

enum.3: Field-weakening (weak-field) mode active; clear = MTPA control
enum.15: Over-voltage condition present (changes fault_status_word bit 4's meaning to Over-voltage)

explain: Global_state2 in the decompiled source: a second 16-bit status word from the id-214 frame, covering field-weakening and walk-assist state.

name: Global status word 3

enum.0: Unconfirmed: an unlabelled red status glyph is drawn in place of the roll-direction icon while stationary (m_roll==0); brake itself is signalled elsewhere (motor_stop_state bit 15, GraphPage.cs#L1777, a different frame's field)
enum.2: BST mode active — drawn as the gear-1 dashboard label 'BST', distinct from the separate 'Display SideStand' menu feature (GraphPage.cs#L4189)

explain: Global_state3 in the decompiled source: a third 16-bit status word from the id-214 frame, driving the gear-1 'BST' label and an unconfirmed roll-direction status glyph.
notes: Fix round 1, findings 1 and 4: an earlier draft mislabeled bit 2 as a 'side-stand alarm' and bit 0 as a 'brake indicator' — neither label is supported by the cited lines. Bit 2 (GraphPage.cs#L3651-L3664) draws the literal text 'BST' as the gear-1 label when Global_state3&4 is set; the app's own multi-function menu (GraphPage.cs#L4189) lists 'Display BST' and 'Display SideStand' as two different features, so 'BST' cannot be renamed 'side-stand'. Bit 0 (GraphPage.cs#L3903-L3920) draws an unnamed red glyph (built from raw canvas.DrawLine calls, no text label) instead of the normal roll-direction bitmap while the vehicle is stationary; nothing in the cited lines names it 'brake' — the app's own brake signal is a different bit in a different frame (motor_stop_state & 0x8000, GraphPage.cs#L1777).

name: Global status word 4 (unconfirmed)
explain: Global_state4 in the decompiled source: assigned from the id-214 frame but no bit within it is ever read anywhere else in the app.
notes: Included for completeness/parity with status_word_1-3, which share the same frame and assignment statement — decode_telemetry returns its raw 16-bit value like any other bitfield, but no bit meaning is documented here because none was found. Do not assume any bit's semantics beyond 'reserved/unknown'.

name: Battery state of charge
explain: Battery state of charge as a single raw byte percentage (0-100), copied by the app straight into App.SOC with no scaling.
source: worthless:jadx/sources/com/rcplusplus/fdandroid/data/FardriverTelemetry.java#L25 (soc: Int — 'state of charge' is conventionally always expressed as a percentage by definition, so the field name itself is the unit; kept at medium confidence on that basis, per fix round 1 finding 3's ruling)

name: Hardware version letter
explain: Single ASCII character identifying the controller's hardware family/revision (App.HardVer), used elsewhere in the app to filter which firmware files apply to this controller and to gate feature availability by hardware generation. Task 8: no WriteAddr call site anywhere in MotorNet6/*.cs targets a register address holding this value, so it does not fit protocol/registers.json's addr-keyed schema; it only appears as extra bytes on this otherwise-throttle_voltage telemetry frame.
source: worthless:jadx/sources/com/rcplusplus/fdandroid/data/FardriverConfig.java#L113 (kzqVersion0: Int, exact field-name match to the official app's own rcv_kzqVersion0 variable name — but declared as a plain Int with no documented meaning, and Task 6 already found no literal register address for it anywhere in Worthless either, docs/decompile-notes.md's Task 6 notes)
notes: This is logical id 130 in ParaPage.cs's FlashReadAddr table (index 25 of 55, ParaPage.cs#L177-184), so cmd = 0x80|25 = 0x99 — the same frame protocol/telemetry.json already documents offset 0 (throttle_voltage) for; offsets 9-11 were previously undocumented/unused in this file. Two independent pages (ParaPage.cs, GraphPage.cs) read this same byte the same way, which is the corroboration for including it despite low confidence.

name: Software/firmware version, major character
explain: Single ASCII character identifying the controller firmware's major version family (App.SoftVer0), used elsewhere in the app (alongside hardware_version) to decide whether the controller needs a firmware update prompt and which mode-select command to send when entering the bootloader (docs/protocol.md §7). No WriteAddr call site targets a register address holding this value, so it does not fit protocol/registers.json's addr-keyed schema.
source: worthless:jadx/sources/com/rcplusplus/fdandroid/data/FardriverConfig.java#L114 (kzqVersion1: Int, exact field-name match to the official app's own rcv_kzqVersion1 variable name — same caveats as hardware_version above: plain Int, no address found by Task 6)
notes: Same frame/id as hardware_version (see that entry's notes) — id 130, cmd 0x99, FlashReadAddr index 25.

name: Software/firmware version, minor sub-version
explain: Raw numeric software sub-version byte (App.Softver1) — unlike hardware_version/software_version_major, the decompiled source does not cast this byte to char before storing it, so it reads as a plain 0-255 counter rather than an ASCII character. No WriteAddr call site targets a register address holding this value.
source: worthless:jadx/sources/com/rcplusplus/fdandroid/data/FardriverConfig.java#L203 (softVer: Int, exact field-name match to the official app's own rcv_SoftVer/App.Softver1 variable names — same caveats as the other two version entries: plain Int, no address found by Task 6)
